bottleneck: AAV-delivered transgenes can be silenced over time by epigenetic mechanisms, and transduced cells are gradually cleared by cellular immunity, so expression that looks durable at one year may fade by year five. Because re-dosing is blocked by anti-vector immunity, waning expression means the therapy's benefit has an unknown expiration date with no rescue option. Long-term follow-up data beyond a decade barely exists for any approved product, so durability is assumed rather than measured.
current_state: Some therapies show multi-year expression; others decline. Lifelong durability — the premise of one-time cures — is still an assumption, not a measurement, and payers are beginning to demand proof.

sources.title: Architecting the Future of Medicine: Precision Delivery

title: Gene therapy durability unknown beyond a decade
why_it_blocks: Patients are asked to accept million-dollar, irreversible treatments on durability data that does not exist. If expression fades, the entire one-and-done economic and medical model collapses, stranding patients and payers alike.
